Each row says what it applies to (replies, yours, older than so many messages) and has its switch and a pencil that opens it under "A display script": "On", "The script’s name", "Its folder", "What it does" ("How it looks", "What is sent", "The message"), "On" ("Replies", "Yours", "Both"), "Only older than" (messages from the end; empty is every one), "Find" (a regular expression, said plainly when it does not read) with "Every match", "Any case", "Line by line" and "Dot takes new lines", "Replace with" ($1, $2… for what it caught, {{match}} for all of it, {{char}} and {{user}}), and "Try it on": paste a reply as the model writes it and see it as it reads, through the same sanitiser a passage uses; nothing there is kept. "Duplicate" and "Delete" (with Undo). "Add a script" adds a display script that does nothing until it has a pattern. "Its own styles": CSS for the passages of stories told with this preset, applied to them and never to the app around them; pictures only from https, and @import and fonts are left out. The prefill is sent only to Claude through Anthropic or an Anthropic-format custom proxy (not through OpenRouter), and not to Claude models from 4.6 on, which refuse it (Haiku still takes it); the margin's "The prefill" says so. "Export and copy": "Export preset" saves the preset as a chat-completion preset file: on a desktop it downloads as a JSON file named after the preset, on a phone it goes to Downloads or the share sheet, and the sheet then says "The preset was exported as a chat-completion preset." Other chat apps that take such presets read it; Aetheria's blocks are left out; the card's picture goes with it and comes back on import into Aetheria. A panel goes as a block with its instruction (kept to its conditions) and two scripts, one that draws it as a fold and one that leaves older ones out of what is sent; its own styles go as a script that puts them before each passage; fields that go to every provider go as the file's "include body". Imported back into Aetheria, these are panels and styles again (the made blocks and scripts are dropped), the request fields arrive switched off, and the house preset is still the house preset, in the edition it went out as. A preset file's lowest reasoning effort, "min", comes in as Minimal and goes back out as "min". "Duplicate" puts a copy on the shelf. At the foot, "Delete preset" (deleting a preset does not alter stories that already used it), or for the default "Reset the default preset". A preset's card can have a picture: "Add a picture" under it in the Library (see The Library).
The house preset

"Aetheria Storyteller" (in a new archive, the one new stories use) and the built-in "Default Preset" (what "New preset" starts from and a reset puts back) are the same preset, its third edition, in small blocks that each do one thing. "The narrator" comes first. Then "━ Your choices" and twelve groups, with one block on in each: "━ Whose eyes?" ("Third person, past", "Third person, present", "Third person, "you" for the body" (what touches your character is told as "you"), "Second person", "First person, as the character"), "━ How do you take part?" ("As your character"; "As the director", where each message says what should happen and the narrator writes the whole scene, your character's words and actions included, carrying each direction out as given: what it says happens, happens, and only what it says someone tries is weighed; "Co-writing", where you can give just the gist ("I turn him down") and the narrator writes it out in your character's voice with the choice exactly as given, and carries them through the small actions that follow, never a decision or a feeling; "A voice in their head", where you are a voice only your character hears and each reply begins with them, in their own thoughts on it: they do what it urges, but may balk, at most once a scene and never over an ordinary request, when it goes against something specific in their description; the choice sets the opening of "The reader's character" and of "The turn"), "━ How long?" ("As the moment needs", "Short and quick", a few lines and never more than about 150 words, "Long and full", at least 200 words and 350 to 600 when something happens; each still follows the moment), "━ How fast does time move?" ("Steady", "Slow", "Brisk"), "━ What is the mood?" ("As the story sets it", "Light", "Heavy and real", "Dark"), "━ How does the world treat {{user}}?" ("Honest", "Kind", "Harsh"), "━ Who drives the story?" ("Together", "The reader leads", "The narrator drives"), "━ How does romance move?" ("As the characters would", "Welcome", "Slow burn", "None"), "━ Do people change?" ("As they would", "Slowly, if at all", "They grow"), "━ Talk or telling?" ("As the moment needs", "More talk", "More telling", at most three or four short lines of speech a reply), "━ How long do consequences last?" ("As they would", "They last", "They soften") and "━ How far may it go?" ("Gentle"; "Mature", where intimacy is written up to the door and picked up after; "Explicit", where everyone is an adult, bodies are real and can be awkward, and nobody asks again once wishes are plain). To change one, pick its answer under "Your choices" in "What it says" (or switch that block on and the one that was on off); a group left with none on keeps its usual (the first in each group, and "Mature" for how far). Then "━ Which tones? (pick any, or none)", fourteen switches, all off at first, that can be on together: "Wry", "Tender", "Eerie", "Melancholy", "Tense", "Whimsical", "Gritty", "Romantic", "Cosy", "Lyrical", "Frightening", "Mysterious", "Plain", "Epic"; each says what it does to a scene (eerie: one thing slightly wrong, left unexplained; plain: ordinary things stay their real size) and adds a short reminder to "The turn". With two or more on, one line asks that each have its own moments rather than blend. Under "━ The telling", "How this story is told" reads the choices and tones back to the model and says they outrank the general blocks; only your own directions (((like this)) or OOC) outrank them. Then, on: "The reader's character" (as your character, the usual: never your character's words, thoughts, feelings or choices; what your character only thinks, and any secret in their description, no one in the story hears until they see it or are told; what you attempt can work, cost something or fail; a reply ends where it is naturally your move), "Living people" (each knows only what they have seen or been told, feelings change at a human pace, and people can agree and concede without needing the last word), "When asked for something" (a request gets this person's real answer: yes, yes on terms, a question first, not yet, at a price, prove it, or no with a reason; each yes is its own, and someone pressed on a real limit offers something smaller rather than giving in), "What people keep back" (secrets stay hidden by default and leak sideways under pressure; nobody keeps re-asking after you dodge a question), "What a moment leaves" (a reaction happens once, then people drift back to their usual manner while the effect stays; hard things can stay hard, with no lesson or silver lining), "How people talk" (voices from each person's age, trade and place; feeling breaks a line rather than chopping it into fragments; people answer heavy news as people, not counsellors), "Under the words" (people answer what lies under a line in how they reply, and nobody names it unless to confront it), "True to the character" (no drift toward nicer or calmer over a long story; a trait shown once is left to work, and the rest of the description comes out over time), "Their own way" (where a card gives someone a way of talking that the general guidance would smooth away, the card wins for them), "Several people" (a scene with several people has a centre, and nobody arrives just in time; sent only in a story with several characters, from any copy of the house preset), "New people, new names" (someone already in the story before anyone new; a newcomer arrives mid-day with a reason; names that fit their place and era, never sharing a first name with someone already there, and passers-by can stay nameless), "Consequence and continuity", "Where the reader points" (it stays when you linger and cuts ahead when you skip), "Prose craft" (tests the model runs on its own draft), "Fresh each time" (no echo of your last line, each habit replaced with what to do instead) and "Directions from the reader" (text in ((double brackets)), [square brackets] or marked OOC: a direction is followed without comment until you lift it; a question gets a short answer in ((double brackets))). Just before your own character's description, "Whose description follows" (sent only when you have described them) tells the model the description is for it alone: people in the story know only what they have seen of you or been told. After the history, on: "The model's habits (filled by the app)", a short note on the habits of the model the story uses and what to do instead (Claude's stock idioms and one-upmanship, Gemini's counsellor voice and colourful passers-by, GPT saying a thing twice, DeepSeek wandering from your character, GLM ending on a pointed silence or a filler word, Kimi and Qwen reaching for the most dramatic thing allowed, MiMo forgetting a card's facts, Gemma's outsized reactions, Nemotron's dashes; and for a model that thinks before it writes, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen or MiMo, one short pass of notes, so its thinking leaves room for the reply), sent just before the turn, where it holds; nothing for a model without a note; in another app {{model_habits}} is left as written, so switch the block off there. Off until you want them: "Plain talk (if it sounds like an assistant)", and after the history "Chance decides (a die each turn)" (a d20, rolled before the reply, settles one risky attempt), "Life offstage (a die each turn)" (a d20 decides whether the world beyond the scene reaches in), "Threads come back (a die each turn)" (on 16 or more, one thing the story left open, a promise, a debt, a person, returns and changes what someone wants), "Plan first (for models that do not think)" (a short plan in <think> tags; a model that reasons on its own plans there instead) and "Think briefly (for models that think too long)". Last of all, after the history, "The turn" restates the essentials: how you take part, whose eyes, how long, talk or telling, the tones' reminders, and a first letter for any new name this reply, drawn at random so new people are not always called the same few things. "Post-History Instructions" is empty: it is the slot a card's own fills. Sampling: temperature 1, top P 1, penalties off, 32,768 context and 4,000 response tokens (room for models that reason before they write; "How long?" sets how long a reply is); nothing a regex has to clean up. A preset saved in an archive never changes when the app is updated, the default included: an archive that has an earlier edition keeps it, and resetting the default preset gives this one under the default's name. While the shelf has no copy of this edition (a preset made with your guide does not count), the top of the Presets deck says "A new edition" once: "Add it" files it as a new preset, "Aetheria Storyteller" ("Aetheria Storyteller (third edition)" when that name is taken), changing nothing else, and then offers "Use it for new stories" and "Done"; "Not now" puts the note away for good. A preset file that leaves out repetition penalty is sent none.

A character card's system prompt replaces the Main Prompt block and its post-history instructions replace Post-History Instructions, unless the block forbids overrides; {{original}} inside them keeps the preset's text.

Macros are expanded block by block in order, with one shared context: {{char}}, {{user}} (whoever you play), {{persona}}, {{description}}, {{scenario}}, {{setvar::name::value}} and {{getvar::name}} (a variable set early is read later), {{addvar}}, {{incvar}}, {{decvar}}, {{getglobalvar}}, {{random::a::b}}, {{pick::a::b}}, {{roll::2d6}} (or the older {{roll:2d6}}), {{lastMessage}}, {{model}}, {{model_habits}} (the house preset's note on the story's model), {{time}}, {{date}}, {{weekday}}, {{newline}}, {{trim}}, {{// a comment}} (or {{//}} … {{///}} over many lines). The newer forms work too: {{setvar::name}}…{{/setvar}}, which keeps what is between the tags as the value (trimmed; {{#setvar::name}} keeps the spaces), {{if …}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}, and Lumiverse's {{setchatvar}} and {{getchatvar}}, which are the same story variables, and its {{groupOthers}}, the rest of a group story's cast without you ({{notChar}} names you too). {{description}}, {{personality}}, {{persona}} and the other card macros come with the card's own {{char}} and {{user}} filled in. The newer forms some presets are written in work too (DEUS EX MACHINA throughout): {{.name}} reads a story variable and {{$name}} a global one; {{.name = value}} sets it, {{.name += 5}}, {{.name -= 2}}, {{.name++}} and {{.name--}} count, {{.name == value}}, != , >, >=, <, <= compare ("true" or "false"), and {{.name || fallback}}, {{.name ?? fallback}}, ||= and ??= fall back; {{if condition}}…{{else}}…{{/if}} sends one branch only ({{#if}} keeps its spacing), with ! to invert, and empty, false, 0, off and no count as false. {{summary}} sends nothing, since Aetheria sends its own memory. {{outlet::name}} sends the lore that fired under that outlet's name, or nothing when none did (see Lorebooks, "Outlets"); the classic builder reads it too. Variables are kept with the story from one reply to the next. Unknown macros are left as written, as an extension's own ({{dialoguecolors}}) are.

Regex scripts arrive with an imported preset or card, or are written in "Display scripts" (a card's own are not edited here). A script runs only for its placement (user input or AI output) and between its min and max depth (0 is the newest passage), in the order global, the character's, the preset's. Display-only scripts change what you see, never what is stored or sent. Prompt-only scripts change what the model is sent, and what the memory pass reads; a preset's "Savers" strip old tracker blocks this way. Scripts that are neither rewrite a message as it arrives, as other apps run them, and what they write is what is kept: a reply once it is finished (its thinking by the scripts for reasoning, its words by those for AI output; DEUS EX MACHINA tidies and seals its Momentum routes this way), and your own message as you send it or as "Write for me" writes it. "Write for me" also tells the model that the preset's rules about leaving your character to you are set aside for that one message. A style block a display script writes is applied to that passage only, and the data- marks its rules select on are kept (scripts, event handlers and frames never are). So are the drawings a script writes (icons, dials and portraits drawn in SVG, as Sola V4 and DEUS EX MACHINA do), with their gradients; a drawing can never run script, load anything from outside or animate. Tabs a preset builds from labels and choice buttons (DEUS EX MACHINA's module tabs) switch, and a script's list or heading keeps its class, so its styling holds. A preset without Savers is covered by Workshop → Reading → "Tidy older passages".
A preset like Sola, from scratch, step by step (all on the list builder):

items: Begin: "New preset" (a copy of the house preset, whose blocks already hold a story together), or "Make one with your guide" and say what you want, including what you would switch or set as you go and what should be kept up every reply: your guide drafts the choices, dials, panels and blocks, and the rest below refines it.

Dials, for what you will change as you go: "Add a dial", choose its kind ("Pick one" with its answers for a voice or a mode, "Switch" for something on or off, "Number" for a level). Then either write a block for each answer and set its "When it's sent" to "When a dial says so" with that answer, or put the value into a block's text with "Insert a dial…" ({{.name}}), in a sentence that works for every answer. "Each story can set its own" lets each story choose in its Story Index.

Panels, for what the model keeps up every reply (a HUD, how each person feels, a bond meter, an inventory, a quest log): "Add a panel", name its fields and their kinds, choose what the folded line shows, and leave "The model reads it" on "Newest only" so old panels cost nothing. Give it "When a dial says so" with a switch to let each story turn it off. No regex is needed; the card is drawn in your Binding.
Conditions on blocks: "Kinds of request" for a block meant only for new replies, new takes, continuing or "Write for me"; "Only for characters tagged" for a block meant for some cards only.

State the blocks keep themselves: {{setvar::name::value}} in one block and {{getvar::name}} (or {{.name}}) in a later one, {{if}} … {{/if}} to send part of a block only sometimes, {{random}}, {{pick}} and {{roll}} for chance; "What it remembers" then shows each variable, where it is set and read, and what is worth a look (read but never set).

Its look, beyond panels: "Display scripts" turn a tag the model writes into styled text (for coloured speech, "Find" <coral>(.*?)</coral> and "Replace with" a span with a colour; "Try it on" shows it), and "Its own styles" holds the CSS for the classes those scripts write. A script under "Change what is sent" with "Only older than" keeps old tags out of what the model reads.
Provider settings Aetheria has no switch for: "Extra request fields" (Gemini's service_tier "flex", OpenRouter's provider order).

Try it: in a story, the Story Index meter and "Preset, in the story" show what it sends; switch dials there and watch the cost change. "Export preset" shares it with all of this kept (other chat apps get the panels as scripts).

blocks.text: From the story

Story Index → "Preset" → "Quick edit": pick a "Prompt entry" and change its text (this edits the preset itself, for every story on it), and set "Temperature" and "Response length" for this story only ("Use the preset's" goes back). "Preset, in the story" lists the preset's blocks sent among the latest passages; change those in the preset. Editing a preset calls no model; its blocks cost tokens in every request.

pages.title: Memory
pages.summary: What a story remembers: facts, people, events and scenes learned by the memory pass, how they are recalled, and what it costs.

blocks.text: Story memory is what a story remembers beyond the passages sent as written. Each story keeps its own, read across all its chapters: the chapter so far (a rolling summary), durable facts, the people, places and groups met as they stand now (who, last seen, how they are, what they carry and wear), ties between two of them, events, and where each scene began.
Workshop, Memory

The room opens on a plate saying what is happening: "On" or "Off", how often memory is written and on which model (for example "Every 4 of your turns, each story’s memory is written on the story’s own model, as everything else is. New stories begin on Nemotron 3 Ultra."), with the switch "Remember as the story goes" beside it; "Open the memory workspace" is at the top. Off, the plate says stories learn nothing new and what they hold is not sent with replies; nothing is deleted. One card, "How it remembers", holds the settings: "How often it reads back", "Which model" and "How much it may add to a reply". A margin lists "In this room" and says "What it costs", "What it reads" and "Where you see it" (on a phone it comes after the card). "The Observer’s own memory" is folded to one line with its state ("On" or "Off").
The memory pass

With "Remember as the story goes" on (the default), a pass runs in the background after a reply has finished, once enough of your turns are kept and unread. It counts your turns: the messages you send on the path you are reading. Replies do not count, however many characters answer, so a story with several characters is read no more often than one with one; nor do takes, which are the same turn written again, nor turns on a branch you left. "How often it reads back": "Often · 2", "Every 4" (the default), "Seldom · 8", or "Other", which opens "Read back every 4 of your turns" (the number as set), a slider from 1 to 20. (Before 1.6.2 it counted kept passages, replies included; a number you had chosen is halved into turns, and the old usual of 6 became the new 4.) If you only press send with nothing written while characters answer, a pass runs anyway once 40 passages are waiting. A passage is kept once the story moves on from it, so the newest passage waits (until the chapter closes) and a take you swipe away is never learned. Each pass is one request to the memory model. Its instructions come first and are the same every pass, so a provider that keeps an unchanged start can reuse them (Claude and Qwen are told to keep them; see Providers, "Saving money"). Then the chapter summary, what is remembered on this path (in a long story, past 180 facts, only the facts about who and what the new passages name, whoever is in the story, any pinned, and the latest 40), and last the new passages, up to three times your turns between passes. Passages hidden from the model are skipped; a passage's More menu has "Start memory here" to leave a prologue unread. Editing a read passage sets aside what was learned from it and reads it again.
Which model

The "Which model" row names the model memory uses now ("Same as everything else: each story’s own. New stories begin on …", "Same as everything else: …" or "Its own, for remembering alone: …"). "Choose another" ("Change" when it has its own) opens "Use the same model as everything else" (on by default), which runs memory on the model chosen for everything else, the story's own unless you chose another under "Everything else" (a story's Models sheet, or Workshop → Providers; see Providers). Turn it off to choose a "Memory provider" (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Kimi, Custom proxy) and a "Memory model" id; until both are set, the model for everything else is used. "Fold it away" closes the choice. The same choice is "Remembering" under "Everything else". Local servers are not offered there, but a story on a local model remembers on it for free. The memory model also serves "Read and consolidate" at chapter close, the stewards, a side scene's "End and remember" and campaign recaps.

Recall costs nothing: no model call, no embeddings. Each request carries a memory block inside the history, two passages from the end: the story's page, notes switched into context, "This chapter so far", the scene, "Who's who" and "Between them" (whoever is named in the latest passages or present), "Lately" (recent events), then what is known: pinned facts first, then facts about those named or present. An unpinned fact about no one named or present is not sent. "How much it may add to a reply" (the recall budget: "Up to 1,500 tokens" by default, a slider from 400 to 6,000) caps the block; notes are never cut. A fact or tie "Known only to" some is a secret, sent only while one of them speaks, or to a cast member set to "Every secret". Everything learned is tied to its passage and take: on another take or branch it stops applying.

The Memory deck (Library, Memory; also "Open the memory workspace" in Workshop, Memory) shows one story at a time, plus "How memory works" (the same card, "How it remembers", with "Remember as the story goes" at its head). "Remember now" runs a pass at once; it shows while the story's newest chapter is loaded (on a phone, when that chapter is the one open), and if passages are left unread it says to run it again. "Search memory" finds anything in the story's memory. Tabs:

items: "Facts": the chapter summary ("Edit summary") and facts marked Secret, Pinned or By you. Select one to edit "About", "Kind", "Fact", "Known only to", "Pinned" (always recalled), see "Where it came from", or "Forget fact" (hidden, restorable; nothing is deleted). "Show forgotten, corrected, edited and off-path facts" brings the hidden ones back into the list, each with "Restore fact". "Add fact" adds a pinned fact for every path.

"People & places": "Add someone"; "Keep" beside a field stops passes changing it; renaming applies in every chapter; "Add how they stand with someone". "Forget" followed by their name hides someone everywhere in the story; they come back from the "Forgotten" list with "Restore", or when the story names them again.
"Events": "Add event"; "Major" events are recalled as lately, whoever is present. "Forget event" hides one; "Show forgotten and edited events" lists them to restore.
"Scenes": correct where, when and who; "Not a new scene" sets one aside.

"Stewards": choose among "The lorebook keeper" (drafts entries for what your lorebooks do not cover), "The card auditor" (proposes card changes where the chapter changed someone) and "The continuity checker" (lists where the chapter disagrees with the story); all are off until chosen. "Ask the stewards" reads the newest chapter, one memory-model request per steward chosen. Each draft has "Keep" and "Leave" ("Dismiss" for the continuity checker); nothing is kept until you keep it.

blocks.text: Under a passage, a "Remembered" note shows what was learned from it; pressing it opens the Memory deck. "Remember this passage" in its actions pins the passage itself as a fact, free. The Story Index's "Memories" row shows the counts, "Memory passes" (last pass, passages waiting) and the same switch.

A living character set to revise "On reflection" (or "Both") is revised by the same pass, and a bound world watching with memory hears it; neither adds a call. On a phone only the open chapter's passages are loaded; other chapters' memory is still recalled and editable.

"Observer recall" (Workshop, Memory, under "The Observer’s own memory") is separate: the Observer's own conversations, searched for what is close to your question. On the desktop with an OpenAI key saved it embeds through OpenAI (small charges to that key), which matches by meaning; without that key, and always on a phone, it uses a simple local match, free but rougher. A phone also needs "Observer recall on this device", off by default.

pages.title: The Studio: a character by interview
pages.summary: Make a character by answering questions, in stages, or rebuild an existing card the same way.

figures.alt: The Studio, starting a new character

blocks.text: The Studio makes a character the way you would with a patient friend: a line or two from you, then questions, then a card written from your answers. It is not a destination of its own. It lives with the Library, and what it makes goes onto the Characters shelf.

Getting there: the Characters deck's header has "Make one by interview" (on a phone, "By interview"); the command bar (Ctrl K) has "Make a character by interview"; and a character card's reading pane (and its sheet's Live card) has "Rebuild by interview", which starts a draft from that card, or reopens the unfinished one. The Studio's own page lists your drafts, each with "Resume", and "Make one by interview" for a new one; its index keeps "Drafts" and "Saved as cards". A draft is kept as you write, once something is written in it. A character made with your guide in their panel (see "Making things with your guide") is a draft here as well, in the same list: "Edit in the Studio" on their draft card opens it, with every answer and fact.
The stages, shown down the side of a draft:

items: The idea: "Their name" if you have one (leave it empty and the read-back suggests one), and a line or two to begin from, then "Read it back to me". When rebuilding, the field is "What you want from the rebuild", and "The card as it stands" marks each field "Missing", "Thin" or "Has it"; under "The interview will ask about" the topics are chosen from what the card lacks, and you can change them.

Read back: the model says back what it understood, and settles their pronouns (from what you said, or as the name and idea suggest), which every later step keeps to. "Correct it" takes anything it got wrong or missed; your corrections count as your own words. A suggested name has "Use it".

Interview: "Ask the first questions", then "Ask a few more"; a few questions at a time. Answer in your own words ("a line is enough"), "Skip", or "Decide for me". "Draft the bible" turns the answers into facts.

The bible: every fact so far, each tagged by whose it is: "Yours" (you said it), "Written for you" (you asked the model to decide) and "A guess to check" (the model filled a gap nobody asked it to). Edit, remove or confirm each one ("That’s right"), and "Add a fact of your own". "Draft more from the interview" asks for more; "On to the card" moves on.

The card: description, personality, scenario, first message, example dialogue and tags. Each field has "Write it from the bible" (later "Write it again") or "Write it yourself" ("Edit by hand" once written). A written draft shows what the house checks found, under "Before it is written in", then "Write it in", "Edit first" or "Leave it", and "Try again"; "Check it against the bible" asks the model to check it too (one more request). The house checks are the same for everything the app makes: stock phrases ("Generic"), dashes used as punctuation ("Dashes"), a stock name nobody chose ("Name"), names borrowed from the house examples ("Borrowed"), {{user}} in a description ("Form"), the same opening sentence after sentence ("Samey"), vague descriptors or too few particulars ("Vague"), a length out of bounds, contradictions of the bible's ages and colours, and how little of the bible it uses ("Thin"). The card's own checks read each field against the others: a personality or scenario that says again what the card says elsewhere ("Repeats"); a description with nothing of how they look ("Looks"); the wrong pronouns for them ("Pronouns"); a personality that tells their history instead of how they behave ("History"); a scenario written as a scene, with dialogue ("A scene"); an opening that writes what {{user}} says or does ("Acts for {{user}}"), or never turns to {{user}} ("Opening"); and tags that are phrases or details rather than shelf words ("Form"). When it finds something a second try can fix, "Fix what was found" writes the field again with only those to change (one more request). A field written from facts that have since changed says so: "Rewrite" it, or "Keep as it is". "On to finishing" moves on.
Finish: "Save as a card" (when rebuilding, "Update <name>" or "Save as a new card instead"; a field left empty keeps what the card has). Then "Open the card" or "Begin a story with them".

blocks.text: What it costs: every step that asks the model is a button you press, with the model's name beside it. A field's request also carries a few passages from the starter set as examples of the standard, with the rule never to use them as material; they are the same for every field, so a provider that keeps an unchanged start (Claude, directly or through OpenRouter) reads them back for about a tenth of the price after the first. What each request used is kept on this device. Each has a fold, "What this sends", that shows the request (and about how many words) before you press, and "Stop" ends one that is running. The model is your story model unless you choose another in the draft's panel ("The model it asks"); the only other choice is the memory model, when Workshop, Memory uses one of its own. With no model for stories, the steps say "Choose a model for stories in the Workshop first." Nothing runs on its own.

Why the tags matter: a card is read in every story it enters, so a guess nobody checked is read forever. The bible is kept with the card, so it can be rebuilt by interview later. "Put this draft away" removes the draft, its interview and its bible, after you confirm with "Put it away"; it cannot be undone, but a card already saved from it stays on the shelf. A persona rebuilt here (from its "Picture and full card") is a character once saved: it leaves You for Library → Characters, the same card, so every story with them keeps them.

pages.title: Making things with your guide
pages.summary: Making with your guide: characters, openings for a card or the table, worlds, lore, a look over a card or a story, campaigns, presets and Bindings.

blocks.text: your guide makes things with you in their panel, each as a draft you keep or leave: a character, a new opening for a card you have, a world, lore (for a card, or from a line), a look over a card, a look over the story open now, a campaign (see Campaigns), a preset, and a Binding (a look for the app; see Appearance). "Make something" lists the nine as "What to make", your guide's leaning first: Ilario offers "An opening" first, Maelis "A look over a card", and "A campaign", "A preset" and "A Binding" come last for both ("A look over this story" waits for a story to be open); both make all nine, and "Make one with your guide" in the Library opens on "A character" (on the Characters deck) or "A preset" (on the Presets deck). Asked in words, their answer carries a button for the one you meant ("Make it", "Write the opening", "Make the world", "Write the lore", "Look it over", "Look over the story", "Set up the campaign", "Make the preset", "Design the look"), which opens "Make something" on it.
A character

your guide can make a character with you. It is the Studio's interview (see the Studio's page) asked for you: you give a line or two, answer a few questions or hand them back, and they writes the card. Nothing enters the archive until you press "Keep".
A persona, filled out

In You, under a persona, "Fill them out with your guide" opens this panel on it ("Filling out a persona"). They reads who they are back, asks a few questions about what a character has and the persona lacks, then writes only the parts that are empty: what you wrote of them stays as you wrote it. "Keep: make them a character" writes it into the same card, which moves to Library → Characters, so every story that played the persona still has them; "Edit in the Studio" and "Leave" work as for a new character.
Where to begin

"Make something" at the foot of their panel, beside "Clear"; "Make a character with me" among the starter questions while the conversation is empty; on the Characters deck's head in the Library, "Make one with your guide" ("With your guide" on a phone), which opens their panel on it. Or ask them in words ("make me a smuggler with a conscience"): their answer carries a "Make it" button that begins with what you asked.
The "Make something" card

Choose what to make (see above); for "A character", "Who they are", a line or two, and "Their name (or leave it to me)". "Made with" chooses the model: the model for everything else (the story model, unless you chose another under "Everything else"; see Providers) unless you choose another here, from the memory model (where one is chosen apart from it, in Library → Memory), the models you used lately, or "Another model…", a provider and the model's name as the provider writes it, then "Use it". The choice is kept for the next making; a making already begun keeps asking the model it began on. The card says which model it asks and how many requests ("Asks …: 9 to 15 requests, nothing kept until you say."), with "Begin" and "Not now". With no model set up it says so, and nothing can begin.
The questions

They reads your idea back (one request) and chooses up to three questions (one more). The card shows who they thinks you mean, in a line or two, and the questions. Type an answer, or press "Decide for me" and they decides it ("Answer it myself" takes it back). "Write them" writes the character; they decides any question left blank. "Decide the rest for me" hands back every question still open; "Leave" ends it.
The writing

They settles the facts first (the story bible, one request), then writes each part of the card from them alone: the description, the personality, the scenario, the opening (first message), example dialogue and tags, one request each. The card names the step ("Writing the description… (4 of 9)") and has "Stop". Each part is written knowing what the card already says, so it adds rather than repeats, and is read against the house checks (the same as the Studio's: stock phrases, dashes as punctuation, a stock name nobody chose, names borrowed from the starter set, vague words, and the card's own checks: a personality that retells the description, a description with no looks, the wrong pronouns, a scenario written as a scene, an opening that acts for {{user}} or never turns to them). It is written once more when a second try can fix what was found, so a part can take two requests. A reply that comes back empty is asked again twice, after a pause, each time with more room (a model that thinks before it writes can spend its room thinking); one that stops halfway through a sentence is asked again once with more room, and one still cut off ends at its last whole sentence. A suggested name is asked to begin with a letter of the draft's own and never to be one of the names every model reaches for, and the people and places the facts name the same. It goes on with the panel closed.
The draft

When it is written the card shows the name, a line of who they are, the tags, the start of the opening, and what it cost ("11 requests · 21.6k tokens", with the price where the model's is known, or "free"). Three choices: "Keep" puts the card on the Characters shelf; "Edit in the Studio" opens the draft in the Studio, every answer and fact with it, to work on there; "Leave" lets it go and takes the draft out of the Studio too. Kept, the card offers "Open the card" and "Begin a story with them".
Lore for them

Once a character is kept, their card offers to write the people, places, things and customs their facts name ("Write their lore"; one request, and one more if some entries need a second try against the same house checks). Each entry shows its title, "Called up by:" with its keys, and its words. "Keep the lore" makes a lorebook named for them ("Wren Tallis’s lore") on the Lorebooks shelf and binds it to the character, as an imported card's lorebook is bound: "Begin a story with them" attaches it to the story, and on the Table it counts when it is on the bench beside them (see Lorebooks). "Open the lorebook" opens it on its shelf. "Leave it" makes nothing. The character's own entry is never written: their card covers them.
An opening

Choose the card and, if you like, where it begins and how you come into it ("Late at night, I bring in a dog that was hit on the highway"), or leave that to them. They writes it the way the Studio writes a first message, from the card, told the openings it already has so it finds a new place or moment; where you said it begins wins over the card's scenario. It is read against the same checks (it never writes what you say or do, and it turns to you at the end) and written again once when a second try can fix what was found: one or two requests. "Keep it" adds it to the card's alternate greetings, so a story begun with them can open on it as a take; "Begin a story with it" begins one from this opening now, kept or not; "Write another" writes a different one; "Leave" keeps nothing.
An opening for the table

On the Table, "An opening from your guide" (once the bench holds more than one character, or one with a lorebook or a world) hands them everything on it: the characters, lead first; who you play (that character is written only as you, never by name, with no lines or acts of theirs); the lorebooks' entries, always-on ones first, up to ten; and the world's book. They writes one scene in which they all meet, in the world, where their situations cross (people from different places meet the way such people could, not by magic unless their cards are magical), giving each of them a line or an act, and ending turned to you. It is read against a first message's checks, and against two of its own (everyone not played is named in it; the one you play is never written by name), and written again once when a second try can fix what was found: one or two requests. "Begin with it" begins the story from the bench with it as the first passage (from the Table, with the same cards on it: elsewhere it takes you there first); "Keep it with <lead>'s group openings" adds it to the lead's group greetings (or their alternate greetings, when only one character is in the cast), which a story with them all on the table opens on; "Write another"; "Leave".
Ideas
With "What you enjoy" switched on (Workshop → About), "Make something" also has "Suggest something": three ideas from the lines kept there, each with "Make it" (see "What you enjoy").
A world

A line or two about the place ("A fishing town on a sea loch where the herring have stopped coming"). They says it back with a name for it and how much the map covers (a town, a district, a region or a country), and asks up to three questions only you can answer (what is wrong there now, who holds power, what people come or leave for); answer them or press "Decide for me", then "Write it". They writes its Descriptive Book, the land as a reader would see it and where each place stands from the others, read against the house checks; then the world compiler (the same one as "Build the world" in the world's Book) draws the map from it. Three to five requests, one of them long; on a slow model it can take several minutes. The draft shows the name, the book ("Read it all"), the places on the map, and anything the map could not place as the book says. "Keep the world" builds it and puts it on the Worlds shelf; "Open the world" opens it (which turns on "Worlds in stories"), where its book can be changed and built again like any other. "Write it again" writes a fresh book and map; "Leave" keeps nothing.
A preset

A line or two about how your stories should be told ("Hard-boiled noir in a rainy city: clipped talk, a cynical narrator, nobody clean"). They says it back, sets the house preset's twelve choices to match it ("Whose eyes", "How you take part", "How long", "How fast", "The mood", "How the world treats you", "Who drives", "Romance", "Do people change", "Talk or telling", "Consequences", "How far it may go", and how bold the wording is), names what else you asked for that the house preset does not already cover, and asks up to three questions about the telling (never about names, a cast or who you play: a preset serves every story told with it). Where your own words ask for them, they also proposes up to three dials (something you will switch, choose or set as you go: "a voice I can switch between snarky and gentle" is a pick with those answers, "let me turn the HUD off" a switch, "from mild to brutal" a pick or a number) and up to two panels (something kept and shown every reply: the day and place, how each person present feels, a bond meter, an inventory, stats), each a line on the card ("A dial: …", "A panel: …") with a switch to keep it; a panel can wait for a switch dial. Nothing is proposed that you did not ask for. Change any choice there, answer or press "Decide for me", then "Write it": they writes a block for each thing asked, at most four, each about one thing and read against the rules a preset block keeps (no writing your character for you, no lists of phrases to avoid, no point of view or length set twice, no names or setting of its own, nothing that needs code, nothing a panel already keeps, no macro but {{char}}, {{user}} and the preset's own dials), and writes again once what a second try can fix. A block can read a dial ({{.name}}) or wait for one: a pick about how the story is told usually gets a block for each answer, each sent only while it is chosen. Two or three requests. The draft shows the choices in a line, the dials, each panel with its fields, each block with what it is for (and "Sent only when …" for one that waits), and about how many tokens they add to every request, the panels' instructions included. "Keep the preset" files it on the Presets shelf: the house preset under its new name, the choices set, the dials and panels kept, the blocks after "Directions from the reader" with their conditions, and the temperature its wording asks for (steady 0.8, balanced 1, bold 1.15). Each story then sets its own dials and how its panels show, in its Story Index. Then "Use it in this story" (when a story is open, from its next reply), "Use it for new stories", or "Open the preset", where it can be changed like any other. A made preset reads up to 32,768 tokens of a story, as the house preset does; when the story's preset before read more, the card says so (memory carries what falls out, or let it read more under "How it feels" in its sheet). "Write it again" writes fresh blocks; "Leave" keeps nothing. "Make one with your guide" at the head of the Presets deck opens "Make something" on "A preset".
Lore

"For a character" writes entries for the people, places and things a card names (as "Write their lore" does for a character they made); "From a line" ("A drowned town whose bells ring at low tide") writes the people, places, things and customs a story set there would bring up first, and names the book. One request, and one more when some entries need a second try. The entries show with their keys; "Keep the lore" files the lorebook on the Lorebooks shelf, bound to the character when it is for one; "Write it again" asks for a fresh set.
A look over a card

Choose the card and "Read it": the Studio's checks read every part of it (stock phrases, dashes, stock names, a personality that retells the description, a description with no looks, the wrong pronouns, a scenario written as a scene, an opening that acts for {{user}}, tags that are phrases, lengths), and no model is asked, so it costs nothing. What a second try can fix is starred. "Fix what was found" writes those parts again, changing only what was found (one or two requests a part, knowing the rest of the card), and shows the new words beside the old, each with its own switch; "Keep the change" (or "Keep 3 changes") writes the ones switched on to the card, and "Leave the card as it is" changes nothing.

A look over this story (with a story open; Maelis offers it second, Ilario after a look over a card). "Read it" sends one request: the chapter so far (its newest 80 passages, or fewer when they are long), the cast's cards, their lorebooks' always-on entries and the entries the chapter names, and the notes the story already keeps in its context. They reads it the way a careful editor does and reports what it has let slip (a name, a number, an injury, an object, the time, who is where, what someone knows, or what a card or the lorebook says that the story breaks), each quoted in the passage's own words with its number, and threads it set up and then left (a promise, an unanswered question, someone who left, an object that mattered; never the story's main question or the last three passages). A slip whose words are not really in the chapter is left out. Each slip offers "Mend the passage" (the AI's own passages only, with the new words shown; only the quoted words change) and "Keep it straight" (a note); a slip in your own passage is told, never mended. Each thread offers "Bring it back" (a note asking the narrator to return to it). The AI's slips start chosen; your own and the threads wait for you. "Make 3 fixes" (or "Make the chosen fix") mends the passages (a passage changed since is left as it is) and keeps the notes on the whole story, switched into its context, so they go with every reply from the next; they are in the Map's notes ("✎ the story"), where they can be changed or switched off. "Read it again" reads the chapter afresh; "Leave it as it is" changes nothing. One request, and a large one for a long chapter: on a slow model it can take a few minutes.
Stopped or wrong

"Stop" leaves it where it was, with "Try again" and "Leave". "Try again" takes it up there: the questions again, or the writing, keeping the facts and every part already written, so only what is missing is asked for. Tags that will not come (asked twice) are left empty for the Studio rather than stopping the character. If something goes wrong (a key refused, a model unavailable) the card says why in plain words, with the same two. If the app closed while they was working, the card says it was interrupted, with "Try again".

What it sends, and what is kept. The same as the Studio: your idea, your answers and the facts, and with each part a few passages from the starter set as examples of the standard (never to be used as material); a provider that keeps an unchanged start reads those back for less after the first. It asks the model shown in "Made with". The draft is kept in the Studio's list of drafts as it goes; the card stays in your conversation with them, and a line saying how the making stands is part of what they is sent when you ask them something next. What each request used is kept on this device.

pages.title: What you enjoy
pages.summary: What your guide thinks you enjoy: off until you turn it on, kept on this device, each line removable; and the ideas it gives.

blocks.text: "What you enjoy" is your guide's map of what you like to play, kept so a suggestion can grow from what you love. It is in Workshop → About, under the guide's own settings, headed "What your guide thinks you enjoy". It is off until you switch on "Let your guide learn what you enjoy", and it is kept only on this device (in a file of its own beside your memories); it never syncs.

How its lines are made. Switched on, the app counts what is already in your archive, with no model asked: the tags of the characters you play with most (weighed by how much you have written with them), the characters you return to and your favourites (starred on the Characters shelf), how long your stories run (or how often they stop early), and how often you ask for another take. Each line says what it rests on ("3 stories, 250 passages, with Aimi and Thorne"), marked "Counted". The starter set and the sample stories are left out: they are the house's, not your taste. "Count it again" brings the counted lines up to date with your archive.
Your hand on it

Every line has "Remove", and a removed line stays gone when it is counted again. "Add it" puts a line of your own in your words, marked "Yours". "Forget all of it" (asked twice) empties the map and switches it off.
Reading it with your guide

"Read it with your guide" first shows exactly what it would send: the counted lines, and a short summary of where each of your most-played stories stands (up to six, from story memory). "Send it" asks your own model once; they adds three to six finer lines (themes, kinds of character, dynamics, tones), marked "your guide thinks", each saying which story or line it comes from. Reading it again replaces the last reading. Nothing is read without your "Send it".
Ideas

With the map on, "Make something" in your guide's panel has "Suggest something", and on a desktop the Table's head has "An idea from your guide" (with no story loaded). Either asks your model once, sending only the lines you kept and the names of the characters on your shelf, never a story. They answers with three ideas: two more of what you love, one a step to the side, each saying which line it grows from and what it would be (a character, an opening for a card you have, a world or lore). "Make it" opens "Make something" on that idea; "Three more" asks again; "Done" closes it.

pages.title: Importing
pages.summary: Intake, the one door for files: character cards, lorebooks, presets, chat exports and personas, each identified and filed in the right place.

blocks.text: Intake is the one door for bringing files in. It opens from "Import" in the rail (desktop), from "More", then "Import", on a phone, from the "Import" button at the top of the Characters, Lorebooks, Worlds and Presets decks, and from the command bar (Ctrl+K, "Import…"). It is a sheet titled "Intake": drop a file on its dashed area ("Drop a file") or press "Choose a file". One file at a time, except a persona file with its pictures (below); drop several and only the first is read. Importing never calls a model. On a phone "Choose a file" offers any file: a phone's picker goes by file type, and a CHARX, a chat export or a world package has none, so Intake works out what each one is, as for a dropped file.
What each file becomes:

items: .png: a character card (PNG V2 or V3, as card sites and other chat apps make them), filed into Characters.
.charx: a character card (CHARX v3), into Characters, with its portrait from the card's own images.

.json: Intake looks inside. A chat-completion preset goes to Presets (one saved by Lumiverse too: its blocks, categories, regex scripts and settings come in as the same preset; where it leaves the reply length and context empty, the house preset's are used), a card JSON (chara_card_v2 or v3) to Characters, a lorebook or world info to Lorebooks. A file of a preset's regex scripts on their own (DEUS EX MACHINA ships its scripts this way, beside the preset) goes to the preset that has them: its line names the preset and says how many scripts were updated or added, or that the preset already has them all (the preset's file usually carries them too). If no preset has them, it is not filed, and the line asks you to bring in the preset they came with first. If it cannot tell, it asks "What is this?" ("Character", "Conversation", "Lorebook", "Preset", or "Cancel") rather than guess. Unknown file types ask the same. A preset brought in becomes the one new stories use; its line says "Filed into presets · new stories use it now". A persona backup from another chat app, or that app's settings file, brings in its personas (below).
.jsonl: a chat export, which becomes a new story (below).

.aetheria-age: a world package. Intake reads and checks it, then opens the world workspace (which switches on "Worlds in stories") with the package waiting under "Review": what it is, whether it carries story history or private material, and whether a world like it is already here. Nothing is added until you choose "Add to the library" (or replace, merge or keep both when one is already there). "Import a world…" in the World does the same from a file picker. Packages over 128 MB are refused.

.zip: any .zip is taken for an archive backup ("Backups are restored in the Archive"). "Open the Archive" goes to Workshop, Archive, which restores it and says what it will replace first; "Cancel" leaves it. That includes a plugin package (.aetheria-plugin.zip): Intake does not install plugins. Install one from Workshop, Plugins.

blocks.text: Results are listed under "Filed": a tick and "Filed into characters" (or lorebooks, presets); "!" when only part came in, with why; a cross, "Not filed.", the reason and a hint.
Character cards, finer points:

items: A card with a lorebook inside asks "Import Lorebook?" ("Import" or "Skip"). Import saves it into Lorebooks as that character's own lorebook. If that fails, the card is still filed, marked "!", and the note says to import the card again.

The same card twice: when the shelf already has it (same name, and the same creator, greeting, or much the same description), a notice says "<name> is already on the shelf" with "Update it", for about fifteen seconds. Update puts the new card's writing (description, personality, scenario, greetings, examples, system prompt, creator notes, tags, lorebook) and, where it can, its portrait onto the one you have, which keeps its stories, its favourite star and how it plays; the copy is then removed. Ignore the notice and you keep both.

In the desktop app a plain picture with no card inside comes in as a blank character, marked "!": "There was no card inside this picture…", to be written by hand or rebuilt by interview. On a phone it is not filed: there is no card inside it.
On a phone, a card that could not be saved to the device is marked: it will be gone when Aetheria restarts.

blocks.text: Lorebooks and presets are not compared with what you have: importing one twice gives two.

Chat exports (.jsonl). Intake shows "Create an Aetheria story" with counts of "Passages", "Alternate paths" (swipes) and "Speakers found", a "Story title", and "Connect to character": the card that speaks in the story, picked for you when one on the shelf has the same name (import the card first if you have not). "Create and open story" makes the story and opens it; the chosen character speaks under their own name, not the story's title. Swipes become takes; messages hidden in the export come in hidden from the model, as they were: on the page, not sent, and each one's menu has "Show to the model again"; passages by several AI speakers all go to the chosen character; the character's own lorebooks are switched on. Files over 64 MB are refused.

Personas (.json). A persona backup, or the settings file that keeps the same personas, brings each named persona in as a light card of yours: its name, its description, and its title as a tag. Personas go to You (who you play, in a story), not the Library, and the line under "Filed" names them and says so: "They are in You (who you play), not the Library." Their pictures are separate image files, kept in that app's "User Avatars" folder under the names the file gives them: choose or drop them together with the file and each persona gets its own; the line says which had none. Bring them in the same go, because a persona already here with the same name and description is left as it is, picture and all, and the line says how many were. One with no name is left out. Where its words sat in the prompt, its lorebook and the chats it was locked to stay behind. When the file names a default persona and nobody is set for new stories, Intake offers "Play <name> in new stories" ("Not now" leaves it); nothing changes unless you choose it.

pages.title: The chat
pages.summary: Writing and sending, takes and swipes, editing, continuing, the passage's actions, quick commands, and who answers in a group story.

figures.alt: A story page with the opening passage

blocks.text: The chat is the story's "Chat" tab: the passages in one column, the composer at the foot, the chapter path under it.
An empty story says "Nothing written yet"
With nobody cast it says so, and "Invite a character" opens the Story Index at Characters; or simply begin below.
Writing

Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a new line; on a phone Enter makes a new line and you press Send. While a reply is written, Send becomes "Stop writing" (Escape also stops it when nothing else is open); a stopped reply keeps its words, marked "Cancelled". Send with the field empty carries on: a last reply is continued in the same take, a last passage of yours is answered again. "Attach an image" or paste one: up to 6, each under 12 MB. Every send, continue and new take is a request to the story's model (the header's model chip); in a group story, one per character who answers. A line above the composer shows other requests running ("Remembering the latest passages on …", "Then Wren" for characters still waiting to answer, "The Observer is reading").
Quick commands

The star left of the field ("Open commands"), or / in the empty field, opens "Commands": "New chapter", "Generate an image", "Attach an image", "Turn voice mode on" (desktop app only), "Guide this reply" (a note "For this reply only"), "Play as…", "Write as you" (or "Write as Wren": optional "Direction", "Write it" drafts your line with one request, "Done" puts it in the composer unsent) and "Response instructions". Workshop → Reading → "Quick commands" picks which show; commands added by plugins join the list too and are not switched there. There are no typed slash commands. The scroll button beside the star opens "Response instructions": out-of-character notes, saved once and ticked on per story, sent with every reply while on. A new one ("Add") is ticked on for this story at once, the scroll button shows how many are on, and deleting one offers Undo.
Takes

Under a reply, "take 2 of 3" sits between arrows: "Previous response" (wraps from the first to the last) and "Next response", which on the last take is "Generate new response" and writes a new take. There is no regenerate; takes are added, never overwritten. On a phone, swipe a reply left for the next or a new take and right for the previous, once it has two takes. More → "New take with a note…" adds a take written with a one-off note ("Write the take"); the take then shows "Written with a note". A reply whose character's card could not be read (deleted from the Library, or a file that no longer opens) is told by your guide in their place, as the story has shown them so far, and shows "Told by your guide" with the reason. With two or more takes, the star marks a favourite and "All takes…" lists them all, favourites first, with their notes and cost, "Read this take" and "Compare" (two side by side, differing sentences marked). A reply that failed before its first word shows "The page tore before the reply was written." and "Try again"; it may also offer "Open Providers" or "Choose a model", and "What the provider said" shows the error. Your passage stays in the story above it, so the composer is left empty rather than holding it again. A reply that ended with no words says so too. "The model thought, and wrote nothing." means a model that thinks before it writes most likely used up the reply's room thinking (the room is named); with the house preset, while "Think briefly" is off, it also offers "Think briefly, and try again", which switches on "Think briefly" in the story's preset and asks again ("Switch on “Think briefly”" when no new take can be asked); "Try again" is there whenever a new take can be asked (more room is under "The longest a reply may run", in the preset's How it feels). "The model sent back nothing." offers "Try again" and "Choose a model". A reply you stopped says neither.
Branches

With Workshop → Reading → "Swipe branching" on (the default) any reply can get new takes; off, only the latest. Each passage remembers the take it followed, so writing on from an older take branches the story (the map draws it). Reading an older take while the story went on from another shows "Reading take 1 of 3 at Wren. 4 passages continue from another take. Nothing is lost." with "Map", "Return to take 3" and × to put it away.
A passage's actions

On a desktop, under the newest passage and on hover under older ones: "Copy message", "Edit message", "Speak message" (replies, and your own when Workshop → Voice "Read your passages in your character's voice" is on), "Bookmark message" (a mark kept on this device; there is no bookmark list), "Remember this passage" (pins it to memory), "More", "Delete message" (asks; removes it with all its takes, no undo; in a story set in a world, while "Worlds in stories" is on, deleting the newest passage also takes back what it changed there). On a phone, ⋯ ("Message actions") or holding the passage opens a bar of the same. Edit offers "Save (Ctrl+Enter)" (rewrites the shown take, no request), "Save as a new path" (keeps the old words: a reply gets a new take, a passage of yours is answered afresh; shown only while "Swipe branching" is on) and "Cancel (Esc)". "More" holds "New take with a note…", "Hide from the model", "Start memory here", "Play a side scene from here…", "Set when this happens…" and "Share into another story…". A passage hidden from the model stays in the story, but no request or memory reads it; its note "Hidden from the model" has "Show it again". "Start memory here" leaves the note "Memory starts here", with "Start at the beginning" to undo it.
Thoughts

Reasoning folds under "Thoughts". Workshop → Reading → "Show reasoning by default" opens it. With a preset of the app's older kind (the classic builder, or a list-builder preset with no order of its own; not the house preset or an imported one that keeps its order) it also asks the model to put its reasoning in think tags.
Panels

When the story's preset has panels (see Presets), what the model wrote in one is drawn as a card under the passage (over it, for a panel written before the reply), in your Binding, and not printed in the passage: folded, one line of its name and the fields chosen for it; a press opens every field, a list a line each, a meter as pips with its number, a note as a quote. While the reply is still coming, the card fills in as it is written. In an opened card, the pencil beside a field ("Correct …") lets you set it right: "Correct it" writes the new value into the passage itself, so the next reply carries on from it ("Cancel" leaves it; Enter saves a line, Ctrl+Enter a list, Esc cancels). A passage shared from another story has no pencils. A panel the story hides is kept but not drawn; how each shows is set in the Story Index. Panels are not read aloud, and "Copy message" copies the passage without them.
Group stories

With two or more characters, a line above the composer says who is next ("Next: Wren", "Everyone answers, in order", "Whoever you address answers", "Choose who answers", "Told together, as one scene"). Press a name and they answer the next send. The words open the Story Index's Characters ("Who answers", "Speak now"). An empty send lets the chosen or next character carry on. Type @ for names: @Name answers, quiet or not. Under "Only when I ask" your passage waits until you choose. A reply that starts writing another character's lines is cut there ("Set aside: it spoke for someone else"); a scene told together may write any of them, and is cut only where it starts writing yours.

pages.title: The story's Details
pages.summary: The sheet that holds a story as a whole: its name, cast, chapters, the page it keeps about itself, tools, tags, notes, and delete.

blocks.text: Each story has a sheet that holds it as a whole. On a desktop press "The story" in the story's head; on a phone press "Tools", then "The story". The sheet is titled with the story's name, and the same sheet opens from the Stories shelf ("About this story"). The story's head (its name, the model chip, "The story") folds away with the arrow at its right end, and unfolds with the arrow beside the views; on a laptop's short window it folds by itself in the Map and World views, until you fold or unfold it yourself.
What it holds, top to bottom:

items: Counts of chapters, passages and facts remembered, with "Continue" (from the shelf only), "Open the map" and "Lay out on the table" (the story's cast back on the bench).
"Name", and "What it is about": a line for you and for finding it later. It is not sent to the model; the scenario is.
"Who and where": the cast (a quiet character is marked "quiet"), the world, the lorebooks and the scenario.
"People and places" and "Lately", from story memory, with "Everything remembered" to open its memory.
"Chapters": each chapter with its sealed summary; press one to open it. Side scenes are listed after them, with "Play a side scene…" (from the latest passage) when opened inside a story.
"The story as it stands": the page the story keeps about itself, sent with every reply. Living characters and closing a chapter write to it, and you can edit it.
"Show the scene card" for this story, and the switches under "Tools the story can use" (see Story tools).
"A campaign" with "Run this story as a campaign…" (see Campaigns), for a story that is not one yet.
"Notes": for you, never sent to the model.
"Delete story": removes every chapter and passage, and its side scenes, after a confirmation. It cannot be undone.

blocks.text: Edits to the name, the premise, the page and the notes save when you leave the field, and belong to the whole story.

Opened from inside a story, the sheet then has the story's "Tags" and a "Rating" of up to five stars (both shared by every chapter), and the open chapter's summary field. In a first chapter that is "The story so far", carried into any chapter that follows; in a later chapter it is "Carried in from the chapter before", sealed when the chapter began and sent with every request in it. Press "Save details" to keep these three.

The inspector's Details tab (desktop, on the right of a story) opens when you choose something on the map, and sits beside "Observer" (and "World") whenever the Inspector is open; × ("Close the Inspector") puts it away. On a phone a choice on the map opens the same in a sheet. It shows the story at a glance: the lead and who is with them, who you play, the world, the current scene, the tools that are on, what memory holds, what is on the map, and the stories it is knotted with ("Threads", each with "Open"), with "The whole story" to open the sheet. When you choose a passage, chapter or planned beat on the map, the Details tab shows that instead, with "The story" to go back.

pages.title: The Story Index
pages.summary: The context chain beside a story: what is sent to the model, in order, with token counts, quick edits and the cost.

blocks.text: The Story Index is the panel on the left of a story (eyebrow "The context chain"). It shows what the story sends the model with each reply, in the order it is sent, and lets you change most of it in place.
Opening and closing

It starts closed. On a desktop, open it with the "Story Index" door at the left of the story's tabs, or Ctrl+B; fold it with its ‹ ("Collapse Story Index") or Ctrl+B again. Your choice is remembered on this device, and every story opens the same way after. Opening it for a purpose (inviting a character, "Play as…") is not remembered. It steps aside while a portrait is in focus. On a phone it is a sheet: press "Index" in the story's head, or swipe in from the left edge.

At the top, one sentence names the story's makings: "Told by (the preset) as (who you play), with (the cast). N lorebooks · N facts remembered." Each name opens its row. Below it, the token meter shows the request's size against the model's window ("assembled tokens"), split by section; press a segment to open that row. "Last reply" says what the provider reported for the last reply, including what was read back from the cache, and "at the Flex price" when Gemini's half-price tier served it (Workshop → Providers, "Saving money"); when the cache stopped helping, it names the block that changed ("Reuse stops at …"). "What this story has cost" opens the cost ledger: requests, tokens sent, from the cache, written, and an estimated price, then "What it was for", "By chapter" and "By day". "What it was for" splits the story's requests by kind, each with its requests, tokens sent and price: "Replies" (every take, with its tool calls), "Writing your line" ("Write as you"), "Remembering" (memory passes), "Closing a chapter", "Summaries and recaps" (a chapter's auto summary, a side scene's summary, a campaign recap), "Stewards", "The world noticing" and "The Observer" (questions asked while this story was open). Pictures and "Write it for me" are not in it. Requests from before the ledger was kept are not counted.
"Sent in this order" lists the rows, each with its token count:

items: Preset: the preset in use. A story whose preset has been deleted is told by the "Default Preset", and the row says so ("Default Preset (its own preset is gone)"); choose another to replace it. Swap it ("Use"), set the preset's dials for this story under "Its dials, for this story" (each dial a story may set; a change applies from the next reply to this story only, says what the preset has, and "Use the preset’s" puts it back), choose how its panels show in this story under "Its panels, for this story" ("Folded", "Open" or "Hidden" for each, from the preset until changed, with "Use the preset’s" to go back, and the panel's last values in this story), edit one of its prompt entries in place (this edits the preset itself), and set "Temperature" and "Response length" for this story only ("Use the preset’s" puts them back).
You: who you play (see Characters), in a panel of its own (eyebrow "In this story"). Its "Description" edit changes that character's card; "Open full editor" is inside it.

Characters: the cast, who speaks and how they take turns; "Add a character". The × beside a character takes them out of this story (with Undo; their passages stay); the last one can go too, and the narrator then tells the story until someone is invited. The story remembers them: "Earlier in this story" names everyone who was in it and is not now (those taken out, and anyone who spoke in its passages, in this chapter or the one before), with how many passages are theirs and "Bring back", which returns them as they were. The row's line says "earlier:" and their names. Description and Personality edits here change the card itself. Adding a character brings their own lorebooks into the story too (a notice names them, with Undo); take any out under Lorebooks. A character whose card is no longer in the Library, or cannot be read, is told by your guide: the card in this row says so, and each reply they tells shows "Told by your guide" under it.
Living character: only while the speaking character's living page is on; its "Living document" switch.

Scenario: "What is sent" is the speaking character's card's scenario, then this story's own after it. Write the story's own below (Revert and Save); it carries the card's on rather than deleting it. "Replace the card’s scenario" (shown when the card has one) sends only the story's own instead.

Lorebooks: "Add" or "Remove" books, and edit an entry's text in place (this edits the lorebook; the first 40 entries are offered, the rest are edited in the lorebook). Under "In this story", the × beside a book takes it out of this story (with Undo), whether it was attached here or came with a character; the book stays in the Library. Every book in the story is on for the whole story, whoever is speaking; an entry is sent when its keys come up. A book sent with every story says so and has no ×.

World: the story's world (choose another from the list with "Use"); its count is the world's text the request carries, or "not sent while worlds are off", with the "Worlds in stories" switch. A world given to a story while worlds are off waits: a notice says it stays off until worlds are turned on in the story's World tab. Under "In this story", the × beside the world takes it out of this story (with Undo); the world stays in the Library.
Memories: what story memory will add, the last memory pass, and "Remember as the story goes".

Story tools: only while the story has tools on: how many, and whether they go as tool definitions or as markers the model is told about. They are added as the request is sent, and counted in the total.
Preset, in the story: only when the preset places blocks among the latest passages, its panels' instructions included.

Author's note: the story's note. Saving it makes or updates a response instruction called "Story Author's Note", switched on for this story; it is the same list as the composer's "Response instructions". It is sent after the latest passage (depth 0), before the preset's own depth-0 blocks. A planned beat that is due goes out with this row too ("a planned beat").
The chapter so far: the passages sent, lore entries switched in, older passages left out to fit, and the room kept for the reply.

blocks.text: Rows with a Library object offer "Open full editor". A preset may pull the card, or who you are, into a block of its own with macros instead of its markers (Sola V3 does, in its "Oath"): that text still counts under Characters, You or Scenario, and only the rest of the block under Preset. On a phone the Index opens as a sheet headed "The context chain · Story Index".

To fit the window, the oldest passages are left out first; the preset's blocks are kept. By default memory and the world sit inside the history, two passages from the end, so the start of each request stays the same for prompt caching. The sealed summaries of earlier chapters go just before the history.

To see the whole request, press the context gauge in the story's head ("Inspect the assembled request"; on a phone, "Tools", then "Assembled context"). "Context preview" shows every block as a send would gather it, with the model and window: "Cast & you", "Chapter summaries", "System prompt", "Memory context", "Post-history inserts", "Response instructions", "Lorebook" (the entries that fired), "Request messages" and "Advanced", where "Show request settings and raw payloads" shows exactly what goes to the provider. "Your draft" shows what you have typed so far. Opening the Index or the preview costs nothing; no model is called.

pages.title: Chapters
pages.summary: A story is bound in chapters: the chapter path, closing a chapter with its sealed summary, memory tidying and stewards, and deleting chapters.

blocks.text: A story is bound in chapters. The chapter path under the composer sets them in a line by roman numeral, the one you are reading lit; press one to open it, or hover for the sealed summary it carries in (the chapter before's). Beside it are "Open the map" and a chevron that folds the path ("Fold", "Show the chapters"); on a phone it starts folded. The header shows "Chapter N" under the story's name ("Single thread" until there are two).
Closing a chapter
"New chapter" at the end of the path, or in the composer's star commands, opens the "New chapter" sheet ("Chapter III closes · IV opens"):

items: "The sealed summary", carried into the next chapter. It starts from memory's running summary of this chapter, if any; edit it freely. "Write it for me" writes one from the last 50 passages with a request on your default model for new stories (or one picked beside it), keeping only the summary when a reasoning model thinks first; the pencil edits "The summarising prompt", shared by every story.

"Memory": "Read and consolidate" has memory read what it has not read yet, then one consolidation request to the memory model proposes the summary and some tidying: facts to merge or retire, names that are "One and the same", events and scenes to fold together, edits to the story's page. Each is a tile, all ticked at first; the ticked ones apply on "Create chapter". Once read, the button says "Read again".

"Stewards", off until chosen, each one more request to the memory model: "The lorebook keeper" drafts lorebook entries for what the chapter established, "The card auditor" proposes card changes where the chapter changed someone, "The continuity checker" lists contradictions with what is established. They run after "Read and consolidate" or with "Ask the stewards". Drafts wait as tiles ("Keep", "Edit", "Leave"; the checker: "Remember the new version", "Mark as intended", "Dismiss"), marked "Stale" if things changed since. Memory's "Stewards" tab asks them too.
"Continuity": "Open with the last reply" begins the next chapter with this one's last reply. It is on whenever the chapter has a reply to carry.

blocks.text: "Create chapter" opens the new chapter with the story's cast, model, preset and lorebooks.
What sealing means

A chapter's passages are sent only within it. A later chapter sends the sealed summaries of the chapters before it on its path, and what memory recalls, never their passages (the assembled request lists "Chapter summaries"). A summary is kept by the chapter after the one it describes: edit it in "The story" (header) under "Carried in from the chapter before" ("The story so far" in a first chapter), then "Save details".
Gotchas:
